## Step 2: Completing the Application

Students meeting the NYS DREAM Act eligibility criteria can apply for one or more HESC-administered grant and scholarship programs and be directed to the NYS DREAM Act application powered by International Scholarship & Tuition Services (ISTS).

The application is simple and straightforward, and the information provided will be used ONLY to determine eligibility for and administer awards.

Once you have submitted an application, it is your responsibility to monitor its status and ensure its completion. After submitting your application, you will be able to upload any required documentation and monitor its status online.

You will be notified by email when a determination has been made regarding your eligibility for each award for which you have applied. If you are determined to be eligible for an award, your next step will be to accept the award! results.title: DREAM Act FAQs | HESC
results.content:
## When is the NYS DREAM Act Eligibility Application due?

The NYS DREAM Act Eligibility Application is open year-round. Students can apply at any time. However, students must be accepted into the NYS DREAM Act before completing their grant or scholarship application. Since NYS DREAM Act applications typically take two weeks to process, students are encouraged to apply as early as possible to meet grant and scholarship application deadlines.

## Can a student list more than one NYS college on the TAP application?

No. Students can list only one college, which will receive the TAP grant distribution.

## Is completing the NYS DREAM Act portal sufficient to apply for TAP and other scholarships? [...] # DREAM Act FAQs

### General Information

## Is there an age limit for the NYS DREAM Act?

There is no age limit, but applicants must be within five years of their high school graduation date.

## Can international students apply for the NYS DREAM Act?

No, the NYS DREAM Act is intended for undocumented students and specific immigrant categories residing in New York.

## How long does it take for a student’s NYS DREAM Act Eligibility application to be approved?

DREAM Act Eligibility Applications typically take 2 weeks to process. A complete video walkthrough is available for the DREAM Act Eligibility Application.

## When is the NYS DREAM Act Eligibility Application due? [...] Once approved through the NYS DREAM Act portal, students will receive instructions on how to apply for New York State financial aid. They will be able to log into the portal and apply for any open applications they are eligible for.

## Can schools identify students approved through the DREAM Act on the SSL, HESC website, or another report?

HESC does not separate students who apply through the DREAM Act or Alternate Pathway from students who use the FAFSA-TAP pathway.

## Can schools track the progress of students’ alternate pathways applications?

Colleges can review student award statuses after their financial aid applications are approved and submitted on a roster.

results.title: NYS DREAM Act Frequently Asked Questions | HESC
results.content:
# NYS DREAM Act Frequently Asked Questions

## What are the steps to receive financial aid through The Senator José Peralta New York State DREAM Act?

## Is the NYS DREAM Act a financial aid award?

No. The NYS DREAM Act gives students who received their high school degree or GED in New York State and students receiving in-state tuition from SUNY or CUNY, including undocumented students, access to New York State‐administered student financial aid to support their higher education costs.

Students must apply for the NYS DREAM Act, and after their NYS DREAM Act application is approved students may apply for financial aid programs (such as the 2024-2025 TAP award) through their NYS DREAM Act account.

## What financial aid awards am I eligible for through the NYS DREAM Act? [...] NYS DREAM Act recipients are eligible for all New York State Financial aid programs, including TAP, Excelsior Scholarship, Enhanced Tuition Scholarship, STEM scholarship, and all other New York State administered grants, scholarships, and loan forgiveness programs.

For a full list of opportunities available, please visit NYS Grants & Scholarships, or New York State Loan Forgiveness Programs.

NYS DREAM Act recipients must meet the same application requirements as non-DREAM Act applicants.

## Do I need to apply for the NYS DREAM Act each academic year?

Apply for NYS DREAM Act eligibility only once. You do not need to submit this application each academic year.

## Should I or Can I create a new NYS DREAM Act account login with a different email? [...] You can find the eligibility information for this scenario under Section 2 of the eligibility requirements.

## Can I apply for the NYS DREAM Act while I am still in high school?

Yes, you can apply for the NYS DREAM Act while still in high school! In fact, applying early can be a good idea, as it allows you to complete the necessary steps and have everything in place by the time you start college. Your application will still require graduation date verification, but it is a good idea to finish the rest of your application in the meantime.

If the State Education Department (SED) can verify you as a NYS student for at least 2 years, you can continue with your financial aid applications until the graduation date is verified!

# Applying For Aid

### Financial Aid Navigator

### Pathways to NYS Financial Aid

New York State is committed to ensuring all students can access the financial aid they're eligible for. Learn more about the available financial aid pathways to determine which option is right for you.

### FAFSA

Submitting a FAFSA is a key step in making college more affordable. It provides access to federal grants, work-study programs, and federal student loans, and is also used to help determine eligibility for many state and college aid programs.

### NYS DREAM Act

The New York State DREAM Act is a pathway for eligible students who are not legal residents but have a New York high school diploma, GED, or in-state tuition status to receive state financial aid.
